function fibonacci(n) {
  if (n <= 1) return n;
  return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2);
}

console.log(fibonacci(10));
def quicksort(arr):
    if len(arr) <= 1:
        return arr
    pivot = arr[len(arr) // 2]
    left = [x for x in arr if x < pivot]
    middle = [x for x in arr if x == pivot]
    right = [x for x in arr if x > pivot]
    return quicksort(left) + middle + quicksort(right)

User

Can you explain how to implement a binary search algorithm?

Assistant

Certainly! Binary search is an efficient algorithm for finding an item from a sorted list of items. It works by repeatedly dividing in half the portion of the list that could contain the item, until you've narrowed down the possible locations to just one.

Here's a simple implementation in JavaScript:

function binarySearch(arr, target) {
  let left = 0;
  let right = arr.length - 1;
  
  while (left <= right) {
    const mid = Math.floor((left + right) / 2);
    
    if (arr[mid] === target) {
      return mid;
    } else if (arr[mid] < target) {
      left = mid + 1;
    } else {
      right = mid - 1;
    }
  }
  
  return -1; // Not found
}

User

What's the time complexity of binary search?

Assistant

Binary search has a time complexity of O(log n), where n is the number of elements in the sorted array. This is much more efficient than linear search (O(n)) for large datasets.
